texts.1-2: On May 12, 2018, a team takes a small salt-crust sample. It is called S-17. The team carries it to the field tent.
texts.3-5: A signed card dated May 12, 2018 records collection of the sealed salt-crust core S-17 at Glass Salt Flat. The collector checked a box marked TEMPORARY: FIELD TENT. That label names the first stop, not a permanent home.
texts.6-8: This contemporaneous field card establishes the origin and unique identifier of specimen S-17 on May 12, 2018. Its “temporary holding: field tent” field documents initial custody only; it does not preclude a later authorized relocation. Treat this as a dated primary record, not a prediction of the sample’s location eight years later.

texts.3-5: The camp weather sheet for May 13, 2018 predicts severe gusts and heat by afternoon. It advises staff to move delicate study materials away from the fabric tent into a cooler, sheltered spot. It names no person or exact hiding place.
texts.6-8: Issued on May 13, 2018, the archived advisory forecasts abrasive gusts and intense exposure. Its preservation guidance provides a credible motive for relocating the fragile salt-crust core; however, an instruction to secure materials is not proof that any particular worker moved S-17.

texts.6-8: The entry is dated May 14, 2018 but deliberately shifts backward: “Two mornings ago, at first light, the salt crust fractured beneath the corer.” Its narrative date is May 14; the narrated event occurred May 12. This flashback creates an apparent discrepancy only if the reader confuses the date of composition with the time being recalled.

texts.6-8: A legend in the cartographer’s original map identifies a crescent over paired bars as Echo Alcove’s shaded lower shelf; a separate triangular mark denotes the field tent. This fixed legend is stronger evidence than later guesses that the crescent represents midnight or a secret meeting.

texts.6-8: Mara’s authenticated 4:20 p.m. May 13, 2018 custody slip records S-17 leaving the field tent for the crescent-over-bars shelf because gust-driven grit threatened the sample. Cross-referencing the independent cartographic key resolves the destination as Echo Alcove. The slip proves a historical move, not the identity of the person responsible for a different move in 2026.

case.title: The Desert Camp Cipher
case.subtitle: CASE FILE 007 • THE TWO TIMELINES
case.goal: Find who moved the lost research sample in the present, where it is now, and why. Reconstruct the 2018 and 2026 timelines separately, decode the map symbol, and distinguish firsthand records from guesses.

brief.1-2: At Mirrow Basin Ecology Camp, a special salt sample called S-17 is missing from an old tent. Some notes are from 2018. Other notes are from 2026. Read the dates, follow a moon-shaped map sign, and find where the sample is safe.
brief.3-5: At fictional Mirrow Basin Ecology Camp, a rare salt-crust sample called S-17 appears to have disappeared. A visitor checklist directs students to an empty field-tent chest, while an older field journal points toward an unfamiliar moon symbol. Some pages are written after the events they describe. Compare the 2018 field trip with the current 2026 camp investigation, then follow the custody trail to learn what actually happened.
brief.6-8: Fictional Mirrow Basin Ecology Camp prepares to display its original salt-crust specimen S-17, collected at Glass Salt Flat in 2018. A contemporary checklist cites the 2018 field tent as its location, but that chest is empty. The archival notebook uses a flashback; a dated gust advisory precedes a relocation encoded with a crescent-and-bars symbol. The present-day recovery and custody logs introduce a second transfer in October 2026. Reconstruct both chronologies independently, test witness inferences against primary sources, and identify S-17’s latest verified location and the reason for its protective movement.

feedback.who: Separate the 2018 and 2026 moves. Mara signed the May 13 historical slip; the October 9, 2026 transfer form names the technician who physically carried the recovered tube onward.
feedback.where: Echo Alcove is the 2018 shelter and the 9:20 recovery location, not the last verified stop. Follow the 9:40 transfer and 9:52 signed receipt to identify the CURRENT cabinet.
feedback.why: Compare the October 9 transfer reason with the climate readings: the sample needed protection from heat and abrasive dust. A crescent on the old map names a place, not a midnight meeting or evidence of theft.
feedback.proofs: Select BOTH “Lio’s October 9 Transfer Form” and “Dry Archive Intake Receipt.” The first documents who moved S-17 and why; the second independently verifies where the matching tube arrived.

resolution.summary: Two timelines, one intact specimen: Mara sheltered S-17 in Echo Alcove in 2018; Lio recovered it in 2026 and transferred it to Dry Archive Room for preservation.
resolution.outcome: The investigators separate events that occurred eight years apart. On May 12, 2018 the camp collected S-17 and briefly stored it in a field tent. A May 13 gust warning prompted Mara Solis to sign a move to the crescent-over-bars shelf—Echo Alcove. Her May 14 notebook then flashed back to the May 12 discovery, which confused anyone reading page dates as event dates. In October 2026, a copied display checklist repeated only the old temporary tent location. Guided by the authentic map key, Lio Chen recovered the correctly marked sealed sample at Echo Alcove at 9:20 a.m. and signed a 9:40 protective transfer to Dry Archive Room. A separate 9:52 receipt confirms safe arrival in cabinet D-2. Tessa reported an empty tent, not a theft. S-17 was never stolen; a misunderstanding about documents and two sensible preservation moves created the mystery.

timeline.event: The ecology team collects salt-crust core S-17 at Glass Salt Flat and records temporary storage in the field tent.
A wind and heat advisory warns that fragile materials need protection.
Mara signs a transfer from the tent to the crescent-over-bars shelf, identified by the map key as Echo Alcove.
Mara writes a journal entry recalling the May 12 collection—an intentional flashback, not a second sampling.
The display team circulates a checklist copied from the old temporary tent entry.
Lio locates the sealed S-17 tube at Echo Alcove, matching the old transfer and symbol key.
Lio signs the specimen’s transfer from Echo Alcove to Dry Archive Room because the exposed site is hot and dusty.
The archive signs receipt of S-17, seal intact, in cabinet D-2.
Tessa sees the tent chest empty and posts a mistaken theory of theft based on the outdated checklist.
Detectives compare historical and present-day records and confirm both relocations and the specimen’s safe location.
